content.text:
I submitted **index 5 (Sb fraction 0.397)**. Its EQE of 0.042% was the highest of the five compositions I measured. I used all 5 EQE measurements and none of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 0.305 | 0.036 |
| 4 | 0.362 | 0.037 |
| **5** | **0.397** | **0.042** |
| 8 | 0.502 | 0.024 |
| 13 | 0.657 | 0.0003 |

- **Where the peak is:** EQE is best on the Pb-rich side, below Pb₂Sb₂O₇ (Sb 0.5), and falls to almost nothing at the PbSb₂O₆ composition (Sb 0.667). A curve fit through the first three measurements put the peak at about Sb 0.38. Index 4 (0.362) came in lower than index 5, so the true peak is probably at 0.38–0.43. That makes index 6 (0.428), which I didn't measure, a possible slightly better point.
- **What wasn't checked:** The Sb-rich end (indices 14–28, Sb 0.68–0.92) has no measurements. The GP tool suggested going there, but only because it was unexplored. I skipped it because EQE had already collapsed by Sb 0.66.
- **Phases not confirmed:** Without XRD, the link between these results and specific crystal phases is inferred from composition only.
